meta.scope: Suriname batch 2 — Interior/hinterland geography, Maroon and Indigenous populations, labour, education/health gaps, external accounts, and CARICOM. Continues the coast–interior contrast.

candidates.title: Interior districts (Sipaliwini, Brokopondo, Para)
candidates.description: Interior districts that hold the large majority of national land area but a small share of population. Highest concentrations of Maroon and Indigenous communities and of poverty and service gaps.
candidates.notes: Structural geographic contrast. Less than 10% of population but disproportionately high shares of the poor and extreme poor; service access (electricity, water, education, health) is markedly weaker than on the coast.

candidates.title: Maroon population and communities
candidates.description: Maroon (descendants of escaped enslaved people) population statistics and traditional communities, predominantly in the interior. Largest minority with elevated poverty incidence.
candidates.notes: Core identity and social node. Maroons form roughly one-fifth of the national population and a large majority in several interior districts; poverty rates are markedly higher than the national average.

candidates.title: Indigenous population and communities
candidates.description: Indigenous population statistics and traditional territories, concentrated in the interior. Small national share but high local majorities and elevated poverty.
candidates.notes: Complementary identity node. Continuously cited alongside Maroon communities in land-rights, poverty and service-delivery analysis.

candidates.title: Labour force and employment
candidates.description: Labour-force participation, employment and unemployment indicators. Gender gaps persist; skill shortages are a recurring constraint.
candidates.notes: Lived labour market. Employment has recovered toward pre-pandemic levels but female participation remains lower and skill mismatches are cited as a binding constraint for the coming oil era.

candidates.title: Education system — coverage and interior gaps
candidates.description: Education enrolment, completion and quality indicators. National rates lag regional peers; interior schools face the most severe resource and outcome gaps.
candidates.notes: Human-capital node. Secondary enrolment and completion are well below structural peers; interior (Maroon and Indigenous) communities experience the weakest school conditions and outcomes.

candidates.title: Health system — access and outcomes
candidates.description: Public health-system access and outcome indicators. Coverage and quality gaps are largest in the interior.
candidates.notes: Human-capital counterpart to education. Continuously cited for interior service-delivery challenges and for the need to convert future oil revenues into better health outcomes outside Paramaribo.

candidates.title: Balance of Payments / External accounts
candidates.description: Balance of payments and external-sector statistics. Dominated by gold and oil exports; capital account will be shaped by the large Block 58 investment.
candidates.notes: External counterpart of the extractive economy. Gold and oil account for ~90% of merchandise exports; the forthcoming offshore project will dominate FDI and export volumes from the late 2020s.

candidates.title: CARICOM membership
candidates.description: Membership of the Caribbean Community. Primary regional-integration framework.
candidates.notes: Core regional-architecture node. Continuously cited as Suriname’s principal formal integration framework.

candidates.title: Public debt and IMF programme context
candidates.description: Public-debt stock and the macroeconomic stabilisation programme context that followed the early-2020s crisis.
candidates.notes: Sustainability and stabilisation node. High inflation, exchange-rate pressure and debt distress characterised the crisis years; an IMF-supported programme has framed subsequent policy.

candidates.title: District Sipaliwini — largest interior district
candidates.description: Largest district by area; predominantly Maroon and Indigenous population; among the weakest service-access indicators (electricity, water, internet, education).
candidates.notes: Extreme interior node. Continuously cited in district-level service and poverty diagnostics as the clearest illustration of the coast–interior gap.

proposed_edges.basis: Interior districts hold the large majority of Maroon communities.
Interior districts hold the large majority of Indigenous communities.
Sipaliwini is the largest and most extreme interior district.
Education gaps are most severe in interior Maroon and Indigenous communities.
Health-access gaps are most severe in the interior.
Balance of payments is compiled by the Centrale Bank van Suriname.
Debt and stabilisation indicators are central to CBvS and Ministry of Finance reporting.
CARICOM membership structures a portion of regional trade and services flows.
